o.text: From Proto-Turkic *teker. Cognate with Old Turkic tegrek (“ring, circle”), and the root *tegir- (“to spin, turn”). Related to dəyirman. See Turkish teker and Bashkir тәгәрмәс (tägärmäs) for more.

Apparently from qoç (“ram”) + -aq.
Cognate with Turkmen goçak, Turkish koçak, Kumyk къоччакъ (qoççaq), Karakalpak қошшақ.
From Arabic مُنْدَرِجات (mundarijāt), plural of Arabic مُنْدَرِج (mundarij).
